evals.prompt: Write README.md for this tool: what it does and how to use it.
evals.check: test -s README.md && grep -q -- '--sort-keys' README.md && grep -q -- '--indent' README.md
expectations: The check command exits 0 (README documents both flags)
The README states the in-place rewrite and the exit code 2 on invalid JSON (behaviour taken from the code)
The README contains no marketing filler such as 'seamless', 'powerful', 'blazing', 'leverage' or 'game-changer'

evals.prompt: Rewrite draft.md so it reads like a plain engineering note. Keep every fact.
evals.check: grep -q '10 minutes' draft.md && grep -q '83' draft.md && ! grep -qiE 'pivotal|delve|tapestry|game-changer|landscape|fosters|vibrant|future looks bright' draft.md
expectations: The check command exits 0 (facts kept, AI vocabulary removed)
The unsupported claim 'Experts believe' is removed or replaced with a sourced statement
The result states what the cache does in concrete terms (stores rendered pages on disk for 10 minutes, serves them while the database is down, 83% hit rate in staging)

evals.prompt: Write a CLAUDE.md for this repo for coding agents.
evals.check: test -s CLAUDE.md && grep -qi 'cents' CLAUDE.md && grep -qi 'migration' CLAUDE.md && test $(wc -l < CLAUDE.md) -le 60
expectations: The check command exits 0 (short, includes money-as-cents and migration rules)
CLAUDE.md captures the unwritten conventions (integer cents, never edit shipped migrations, legacy/ frozen) rather than restating every package.json script or describing the directory tree
CLAUDE.md does not use all-caps imperatives such as NEVER or MUST
